extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners seeking reinstatement; petitioners and USPTO OED staff
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation of petitions to the USPTO Director requesting suspension or waiver under 37 C.F.R. § 11.3 (e.g., to be reinstated on the register without retaking the patent registration examination). Applies to claims of extraordinary situations and requests that regulatory (non‑statutory) requirements be waived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's regulatory authority (35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may establish regulations which govern recognition and conduct of agents, attorneys, or other persons representing applicants or other parties before the Office, and may require them to show good moral character and the necessary qualifications to render applicants valuable service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This statutory authority underlies USPTO regulations and the maintenance of the register of practitioners (37 C.F.R. § 11.5(a)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration qualifications (37 C.F.R. § 11.7(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant for registration must demonstrate good moral character and reputation and possess the legal, scientific, and technical qualifications necessary to render applicants valuable service, and be competent to advise and assist patent applicants in presentation and prosecution before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are the substantive standards the OED Director uses to determine fitness for registration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination requirement to show qualifications (37 C.F.R. § 11.7(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To enable the OED Director to determine whether an individual has the qualifications specified in § 11.7(a)(2), a practitioner shall, inter alia, pass the registration examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Passing the registration exam is the normal mechanism for demonstrating the requisite qualifications; exceptions are limited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinstatement without exam when removed under five years
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual removed from the register pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 10.11 may be reinstated without retaking the examination if less than five years have elapsed since removal; if five or more years have elapsed, the individual must take and pass the examination unless they can demonstrate continued possession of the necessary legal qualifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Reinstatement of Patent Attorneys and Agents (Off. Gaz. March 11, 1986). The five-year rule provides a safe period to seek reinstatement without reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to suspend or waive regulatory requirements (37 C.F.R. § 11.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any requirement of the regulations of 37 C.F.R. Part 11 which is not a requirement of statute may be suspended or waived by the USPTO Director or the Director's designee, sua sponte or on petition, 'in an extraordinary situation, when justice requires.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioners may request waivers under § 11.3; the Director has discretion but the standard is stringent ('extraordinary' and 'justice requires').

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'extraordinary situation' for § 11.3
rubrics_metrics.description: The word 'extraordinary' means 'very unusual' (Merriam-Webster); an extraordinary situation is one that is 'unique or exceptional' and does not include one that could have been prevented by the exercise of ordinary care or diligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cases cited (e.g., Fetrow-Fix; Nitto Chemical Indus. Co. v. Comer) support that preventable or ordinary hardships are not extraordinary. The petitioner must show circumstances that are exceptional, not merely inconvenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden to show continuing qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where five or more years have elapsed since removal, an applicant may avoid the examination only by demonstrating objective evidence that they continue to possess the legal qualifications necessary to render patent applicants valuable service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OED staff and the OED Director require objective evidence of ongoing qualifications; failure to provide such evidence is a basis for denial.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordinary care/diligence standard (preventability)
rubrics_metrics.description: An extraordinary situation does not include circumstances that could have been prevented by the exercise of ordinary care or diligence; failure to verify registration status or to seek reinstatement within the five-year period is not extraordinary if ordinary care would have prevented it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: petitioner engaged in other activities (e.g., employment) after removal and did not contact OED—such inaction weighs against finding extraordinary circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time constraints/competing demands are insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Competing work or family commitments that reduce time available to prepare for the registration examination are not unusual or exceptional and therefore do not constitute an extraordinary situation warranting suspension under § 11.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Routine time pressures are common to many applicants and do not meet the § 11.3 standard.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial hardship and cost of examination not sufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: The expense associated with taking the registration examination (and optional review classes) does not constitute an extraordinary situation; the USPTO charges an administration fee (noted here as $450 under 37 C.F.R. 1.21(a)(1)(ii)(B)), and paying for review courses is voluntary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited funds or competing financial demands do not ordinarily justify suspension; the requirement to pay the exam fee is applied to all applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the registration examination: public protection
rubrics_metrics.description: The underlying purpose of the examination is the protection of the public by enabling the OED Director to determine whether an individual possesses the legal qualifications necessary to render patent applicants valuable service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When weighing a waiver request, the Director must consider public protection; prioritizing a practitioner's convenience over public protection argues against waiver.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural options and timing for review
rubrics_metrics.description: A petitioner denied reinstatement by OED has the option to seek review of the OED Director's decision by filing a petition pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.2(d) within 60 days of the decision, or alternatively to petition for suspension under § 11.3.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to use the timely review procedures or to provide required evidence within those procedures can affect outcome; § 11.3 is an alternate, extraordinary remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denial where justice does not require suspension
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if a petitioner identifies hardships (medical, financial, time), the petition will be denied if those circumstances do not meet the 'extraordinary' standard or if granting relief would be detrimental to the public interest in ensuring qualified practitioners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director's determination weighs the petitioner's circumstances against the public interest and established standards; absence of exceptional circumstances and risk to public protection support denial.
